lanes.title: Reconcile every prior mobile finding and lead against HEAD 76ace90 and against what is on phones (97b5f15)
prompt: INPUT: docs/investigations/2026-09-02-mobile-checkup-findings.md sections A (17 verified findings + the from_history adjacent observation) and B (every unverified lead), plus the M18 mobile rows in docs/investigations/2026-09-01-m18-verified.json (lanes flows, contract, i18n-rtl, perf, two-lever). The checkup ran at 79a4594, BEFORE M21 waves 2-4 rewrote HistoryScreen.tsx, ResultsScreen.tsx, ProfileScreen.tsx, api.ts, authService.ts, HomeScreen.tsx.

FOR EACH item (number them as the source does): open the cited file at HEAD, find the current line, and record status = still-open | fixed (by which commit: git log -S or blame) | changed (describe) | could-not-locate; record ALSO whether the fix (if any) is ON PHONES (present at 97b5f15) or MAIN-ONLY (landed after 97b5f15) - use git log 97b5f15..76ace90 -- <file>. Re-verify the still-open P1s concretely: image_routes.py metering for authed users; features.ts ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT + LoadingScreenVariants STAGE_CYCLE_MS fake progress; App.tsx boot await on initializeAuth/refreshSession and the axios 120s timeout; HomeScreen compare loader cancel/watchdog; url_routes.py no metering/history/selected_category; version_routes.py force-update dead wire; RevealBurst/PhoneMockup/LoadingRings dead animations; CounterTicker; from_history param on Home smart-pick + Profile; Arabic logout copy; re-entrancy on compare handlers; Results outbound links dead (openRatingSource, price.url); Login back arrow/Email pill no-ops; Step-17 notifications persistence; camera failures silent; expired-token anonymous downgrade (get_optional_user); the 4 first-paint network calls; the 5 unused Cairo weights.

OUTPUT: one finding per still-open or regressed item (dedupe = known:<source id> still-open, with fresh file:line and the phones-vs-main flag), and a single P3 'reconciliation ledger' finding listing every fixed/changed item with its commit. Do NOT hunt for new defects outside this list - other lanes do.

lanes.title: Cold start and bundle size - what the phone loads and waits for before the first useful screen
prompt: STARTUP PATH at HEAD: App.tsx (init sequence, fonts, i18n import(s), initializeAuth/refreshSession, SplashScreen 1.5s floor, preventAutoHideAsync absence, Sentry init, certificate pinning init, feature bucketing, onboarding gate, first network calls) - enumerate every await on the critical path to first interactive frame and every network call fired before/at first paint (the checkup counted 4 incl. a telemetry-only health check and an unbatched analytics POST - confirm at HEAD, list URLs, sequential vs parallel, timeouts). Unguarded awaits before a try/catch that could strand the app on splash. Double i18n import. What happens offline at boot.

BUNDLE (MEASURE): run npx expo export --platform ios --output-dir <scratchpad>/expo-export (and android if time allows) from SmartCompareApp at HEAD; report total JS bytes, module count, and the top-30 modules/packages by size using the source map (expo export --dump-sourcemap + source-map-explorer if installable in the scratchpad, or parse the map yourself). VERIFY the lucide lead: does lucide-react-native's barrel actually ship all icons in this bundle (check the installed package version's exports and Metro's tree-shaking behaviour for it), how many icons are used (grep the 34 import sites), and what a per-icon import or a babel-plugin transform would save - a measured number, not the checkup's estimate. Also: the 5 unused Cairo weights and Geist weights vs app.json expo-font plugin list (assets shipped = bytes on device, separate from JS), image assets sizes, Hermes enabled?, inlineRequires/lazy imports for heavy screens, reanimated/gesture-handler/sentry/i18next/date libs footprint. Every number labelled measured.

lanes.title: Client versus backend contract at HEAD - every call site, every field, every error path, every timeout
prompt: ENUMERATE every network call in SmartCompareApp/src (api.ts, authService.ts, referralService, usage, feedback/events/analytics, share, legal, version, push token, onboarding attribution, contact) - table: client call site x method x path x request fields x response fields READ by the client x timeout x abort x auth header x X-Device-Fingerprint. Cross-check EACH against the backend at HEAD: the route exists and is mounted (tests/_route_introspection.py walker), the Pydantic request model (fields the client sends that the model drops via extra='ignore' - e.g. selected_category on /url/compare - or rejects with 422 - the analytics 422 class), the response shape (fields the client reads that the backend never emits, and vice versa; product.price is an object; overview.confidence shape; usage status fields the paywall/tier gate reads), and the error envelope (parseApiError handling .error vs .detail vs plain axios strings; the INSUFFICIENT_DATA / USAGE_LIMIT / RATE_LIMITED code mapping to i18n copy).

DEEP CHECKS: the 401 refresh interceptor (api.ts) - does an expired access token get refreshed and the original compare re-driven, or does get_optional_user on the backend silently downgrade the compare to anonymous (history + personalization lost, metering skipped)? build the sequence diagram from code; performRefresh success semantics. SSE (ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE default false = REST path on phones): the flag-ON path's terminal latch (complete vs settle_complete vs error), fallback-at-most-once, the certificate pinning behaviour under expo/fetch (documented precondition), the no-timeout on the streaming read. Raw fetch sites without AbortController/timeout (camera identify, social login). Retry policies and idempotency (a retried POST /text/compare = a second paid compare?). Force-update: GET /app/version never called - status. Offline detection and the failureClassification.ts categories vs actual axios error shapes on iOS/Android. Known (status only): M18 MB-contract-01..09, checkup #6/#7/#8/#9 and the expired-token lead - report status with fresh line numbers, then find what is NEW.

lanes.title: Navigation and state machines - dead taps, trapped users, wrong screens, and what a real session does
prompt: ENUMERATE every screen and every navigation edge at HEAD (App.tsx navigators, Stack/Tab params, deep links qaren:// and https://qaren.app/{r,c,q}/ - note qaren.app DNS is NOT attached, so universal links are dead today - what does a tapped share link do on a phone right now?). Build the state machine for auth (splash -> onboarding -> auth -> main; session clear mid-session -> is there a path back to Auth (M18 MB-flows-02 status)? logout; token expiry; account deletion), for compare (Home -> loading -> Results; cancel; timeout; error; INSUFFICIENT_DATA; USAGE_LIMIT -> Paywall transparentModal; re-entrancy double-tap = two paid compares?), for onboarding (17 steps, Step 16 skip when authed, draft+retry in onboardingDraft.ts - what survives an app kill mid-onboarding, Step 17 notifications answer persistence, CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100), for referrals (ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM=true in prod: share sheet -> invite -> landing -> quiz -> register with invite code; Loop 1/Loop 2 toasts; bonus countdown), for history (open -> Results with comparison_id; delete; search; legacy rows), for profile/preferences (EditPreferencesFlow, AI sharing toggle, notifications toggles, push token registration, contact us, legal).

FOR EACH edge: does the target read the params sent (from_history on Home smart-pick + Profile - status), are there no-op controls (Login back arrow, Email social pill - status), silent failures (camera capture errors), unreachable screens, params typed but never passed, and copy-contract violations at the exact site (forbidden EN couldn't/try again/Failed to; AR تعذر/فشل; the Arabic logout confirmation showing deletion copy - status). Also: Results outbound purchase/source links (openRatingSource, price.url) - dead at HEAD? that is a product-critical dead end for a comparison app; the share text content; the min-display floors (1.2s history path). Use the existing jest tests as evidence of what is pinned and write throwaway RNTL probes under the scratchpad for edges nothing pins. Known (status only): M18 MB-flows-01..12, checkup #4/#5/#9/#11/#12/#17 and the flows leads.

lanes.title: Render performance and accessibility on the screens users actually spend time on
prompt: PERF at HEAD: the React.memo/useCallback sweep from M21 W3 - which list rows and heavy subtrees are memoized and which are not (ResultsContent tree during the winner-reveal window, History rows, onboarding steps, Home cards); inline renderItem closures; FlatList/SectionList props (keyExtractor stability, getItemLayout, windowSize, removeClippedSubviews, initialNumToRender) per list; Reanimated: shared values driven but never bound (RevealBurst badgeScale/particleProgress, PhoneMockup glowOpacity, LoadingRings 60Hz setState) - status at HEAD and any NEW dead drivers (grep useSharedValue/withRepeat/withTiming and check each has a useAnimatedStyle/useAnimatedProps consumer); runOnJS at 60Hz (CounterTicker); ProductImage downsampling (resizeMethod, sizes requested vs rendered); expo-image vs Image; heavy work in render (date formatting, i18n t() with interpolation in loops, JSON.parse of full_response on the UI thread in History); setState storms on keystroke; timers/intervals not cleared on unmount; console.* in prod (babel console-strip config) . Measure where you can: render counts via a why-did-you-render-style probe in a jest render, or by instrumenting a throwaway copy under the scratchpad.

ACCESSIBILITY: enumerate interactive components (Button, Chip, IconButton-replacements, pressables in screens) and check accessibilityRole/Label/State, 44pt minimum hit target (hitSlop), Dynamic Type / allowFontScaling behaviour on the emerald headline and Arabic Cairo text (arabicLineHeightMultiplier consumption), colour contrast of emerald #10B981 on white and on black (compute WCAG ratios), reduce-motion respect (AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled) for the reveal/celebration animations, screen-reader order on Results, focus management after navigation and in the Paywall transparentModal, haptics vocabulary (no error/warning/heavy). Known (status only): M18 MB-perf-01..08, checkup #10/#13/#14/#15/#16 and the LoadingRings lead.

lanes.title: Arabic as a first-class user - catalog parity, plurals, RTL mirroring, numerals, fonts, and copy contract
prompt: CATALOGS: src/i18n/en.json vs ar.json - key set equality (count both), empty/identical-to-English AR values (untranslated strings shipped as English), placeholders parity ({{count}} etc.), the 6-form Arabic plural families (zero/one/two/few/many/other) on every site that uses count - list every t() call with count and whether ar.json carries all 6 forms; the intl-pluralrules polyfill wiring in src/i18n/index.ts (loaded before i18next init? Hermes lacks Intl.PluralRules - confirm the polyfill path is what Hermes runs; the eslint import/first warnings there). LITERAL STRINGS: run the i18next/no-literal-string eslint rule count and list any user-visible literal left (JSX text, Alert titles/buttons, accessibilityLabels, placeholder props).

RTL: I18nManager.forceRTL/allowRTL wiring and the restart requirement (does switching language in-app apply RTL without a restart? what does the user see until then?); DirectionalIcon coverage - enumerate EVERY icon render site (lucide imports, custom src/icons, chevrons/arrows/back) and mark mirrored vs not; every style using physical left/right/marginLeft/marginRight/paddingLeft/paddingRight/textAlign:'left'|'right'/borderLeft/borderRight/position left/right - list residuals per file (the M21 W4 sweep claimed 13 sites/11 screens fixed - measure what remains); flexDirection 'row' with order-dependent children and manual reversal; TwoInputShell double-mirror status; bottom sheets, toasts, modals, Paywall under RTL; the onboarding SVG illustrations under RTL. NUMBERS/DATES/CURRENCY: localizedCurrency per locale and its Arabic-Indic digit policy (are digits Arabic-Indic or Western in AR? consistent across price, counts, dates?), BHD 3-decimal formatting, date/relative-time formatting in History under ar locale, percent signs. FONTS: Cairo applied to ALL Arabic text (fontFamily fallbacks per component) and Geist to English; line-height multiplier consumption; text clipping with Cairo's taller glyphs. BACKEND TEXT: the backend returns English verdict/review text to AR users (product lane owns generation; YOU own rendering) - how mixed-direction paragraphs render (unicode bidi marks? textAlign?) and whether error strings from the backend are i18n-substituted or shown raw. COPY CONTRACT grep on both catalogs. Known (status only): M18 MB-i18n-rtl-01..09, M21 W4.

lanes.title: What the 2,320 green jest tests actually protect - contract fidelity, mocks, skips, and coverage of the hot screens
prompt: BASELINE at HEAD (measured after npm ci): jest 242 suites / 2,320 tests pass, 3 suites skipped, 13 skipped + 13 todo tests, tsc exit 0, eslint 0 errors / 152 warnings (baseline/README.txt, jest.txt, eslint.json). YOUR JOB: (1) the 3 skipped suites and 13 skipped/13 todo tests - list each with why and what it would have protected; (2) MOCK FIDELITY: every jest.mock / __mocks__ (reanimated, RNTL host forwarding, expo-* modules, axios, secure-store, i18n) - does the mock's shape match the installed package version's real API? find mocks that return shapes the real module never returns (the Sentry breadcrumb scrub test that tested the PYTHON SDK shape is the precedent); (3) CONTRACT TESTS: which tests pin the backend response/request shapes, and against WHAT - hand-written fixtures or the real Pydantic models? Cross-check 10 client fixtures against the backend models at HEAD (the analytics-422 defect was invisible to tests because the fixture was wrong); propose the mechanism (a generated schema fixture from FastAPI's openapi.json committed in the repo) as a unit; (4) COVERAGE: run jest --coverage on the hot screens (HomeScreen, ResultsScreen/ResultsContent, HistoryScreen, ProfileScreen, PaywallScreen, LoginScreen, onboarding host, api.ts, authService.ts, usage/paywall gate) and report statements/branches per file - name the untested branches that carry user-visible risk; (5) SNAPSHOTS: 44 snapshot assertions - which would catch a regression vs rubber-stamp; (6) the eslint warnings: 80 no-unused-vars (dead symbols - feed the hygiene lane), 13 no-require-imports, 7 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps (each a potential stale-closure bug - review each); (7) CI parity: does .github/workflows/ci.yml frontend-tests run the same commands with the same node version as local (node 24 local vs CI?), and is package-lock.json npm-ci-clean at HEAD; (8) the fact that plurals.test.ts failed on a stale node_modules - is there a guard (engines, a preinstall check) that would tell a developer their node_modules is behind package.json?

lanes.title: The safe-to-remove list for the mobile app, with proof per item - nothing gets deleted without it
prompt: This is the guardrail lane the user explicitly asked for (the prior run was killed before it returned). Produce, for SmartCompareApp/, a list where every item carries a verdict SAFE / KEEP / UNSURE with QUOTED PROOF: (a) components/screens/hooks/utils/icons with zero render or import references - AST or grep across src/, App.tsx, __tests__/, __mocks__/, jest.config.js moduleNameMapper, babel.config.js aliases, app.json plugins, index.ts - and note dynamic requires; (b) exported symbols never imported (the 80 no-unused-vars warnings are a start); (c) package.json dependencies with zero imports (run depcheck or an equivalent under the scratchpad; distinguish runtime deps, expo plugins referenced only in app.json, babel/jest-only deps, and native modules needed for the build); (d) assets: fonts (Cairo weights vs the expo-font plugin list and actual fontFamily uses; Geist), images, the dist/ directory (committed? gitignored? size), __mocks__ for modules no longer installed, orphan snapshots, __tests__ for deleted components; (e) i18n keys in en/ar with zero t() references (static + plural-aware + template families like results.spec.*: mark those UNSURE, not SAFE); (f) feature flags in src/config/features.ts with no readers; (g) the App Store blockers status at HEAD: recompute SHA-256 of assets/icon.png, splash-icon.png, adaptive-icon.png and compare with a fresh npx create-expo-app template's assets if you can generate one under the scratchpad (else state the documented 2026-05-24 result stands unverified); app/legal/*.md still opening with DRAFT?; (h) npm audit 42 vulnerabilities (baseline/npm-audit.json): for each high/critical, is the vulnerable path reachable at RUNTIME on device, at BUILD time only, or dev-only - and what is the minimal upgrade (expo is the only DIRECT high/critical; the axios bump already landed). Never mark SAFE anything referenced by a test that pins a security or contract invariant.

lanes.title: What is on phones versus main, whether the pending OTA is safe, and what blocks App Store production
prompt: DIFF 97b5f15..76ace90 -- SmartCompareApp (6 commits, 38 files, +2,275 -506 per the brief): list every changed file and classify each change as OTA-SAFE (pure JS/TS/assets/i18n), NEEDS-NATIVE-BUILD (package.json native dep added/changed, app.json plugin/config change, expo SDK bump, new permissions, runtimeVersion change) or RISKY-ON-OTA (behaviour that needs a restart or a native side to be present: I18nManager.forceRTL changes, new native module use guarded or not, intl-pluralrules polyfill on Hermes, Sentry config, certificate pinning changes). Decide: is the pending eas update --branch preview from 76ace90 native-compatible with the installed preview builds (compare package.json/app.json/eas.json between 97b5f15 and HEAD; runtimeVersion policy appVersion 1.0.0 unchanged?). List exactly what the OTA would ship (the M21 mobile set) and the user-visible risk of each item on first launch (two-launch propagation).

RELEASE HYGIENE: eas.json channels (development/preview/production; production autoIncrement; appVersionSource remote); the channel trap (installed builds follow preview); CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT=100 and the documented pre-App-Store reset to 10 (is there a guard?); features.ts defaults as shipped vs main (ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT false, others); Sentry sourcemap upload deferred (unsymbolicated crashes today - confirm config); force-update wiring (dead - status); app.json: version 1.0.0, iOS privacyManifests vs the SDKs actually used (expo-secure-store, sentry, google sign-in - are all required reason APIs declared?), ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false (correct given TLS-only?), associatedDomains applinks:qaren.app + Android intentFilters autoVerify with qaren.app DNS NOT attached (what breaks: install-time verification failure on Android, iOS AASA fetch failure - any user-visible effect?), notification permissions, camera/mic permission strings (RECORD_AUDIO requested - is audio used anywhere?). APP STORE PRODUCTION BLOCKERS at HEAD: icon byte-identity (coordinate with mb-safe-hygiene which recomputes SHA), legal docs DRAFT status via app/legal/*.md and legal_routes.py, ASC privacy nutrition label inputs (what data flows exist: analytics events, Sentry, device fingerprint, cohort demographics) - list them as the label would need them, and the Google Sign-In failure on EAS preview (Known Remaining Bugs) - is the diagnostic instrumentation still in the shipped path? Known (status only): M18 MB-two-lever-01..09, #119 done.

synth: Answer for the founder: (1) Is the mobile app in shape TODAY - two answers, one for the bundle ON PHONES (97b5f15 preview OTA) and one for MAIN (76ace90) - and what does the pending eas update --branch preview change, is it native-compatible, and what is the first-launch risk list? (2) Which prior mobile findings are still open at HEAD (the reconciliation ledger) and which were closed by M21 - so the stale ones are killed for good. (3) The measured bundle picture and the biggest verified size win. (4) The SAFE-TO-REMOVE list for the mobile app as APPENDIX A (SAFE only; KEEP/UNSURE in APPENDIX B) - the user's rule is nothing is deleted without it. (5) The App Store production blocker status (icons, legal, privacy labels, Google Sign-In). (6) The Arabic user's experience end to end (rendering side; the product lane owns generation). Units: client-side changes ship UNFLAGGED by nature but reach phones only via OTA - every unit must say OTA-safe or needs-build, and the backend units (camera/url metering) must carry the usage-gate tests-first list.
